title: metadata-protocol: a delete naming one package with `dropStorage=true` drops the object table while another package row of the object remains — the remaining package object loses its data
body:
Filing gate ①, **data-integrity**: a reachable defect that destroys data, measured at a public door. Filed by `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · `huangyiirene` · session `session_01YRp5z4kK6vgYkrdH97ztsy`, from #23297's dev report (`os-dev-report` on #23297, out-of-scope finding 1; PR #23408). ⛔ Not a claim. Grade and lane are triage's.

**Reader who acts:** triage, to grade and route (the data-integrity path). Then the owning seat. The landing point is `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` `deleteMetaItem`'s storage drop (`shouldDropStorage` → `dropObjectStorage`).

## What happens (measured)

On a booted showcase at the #23297 branch tree (`ae6b35c16`, `main` `e4ec6ec1a` merged):
1. Package `com.qa.p` and package `com.qa.q` each hold a row of the object `qa_probe_drop`. A record of the object exists.
2. `DELETE /api/v1/meta/object/qa_probe_drop?package=com.qa.p&dropStorage=true` answers `200`. Its receipt says the item still exists and its row bound to `com.qa.q` remains.
3. `GET /api/v1/data/qa_probe_drop` then answers `500 DATABASE_ERROR`: the table is gone, and the record created before the delete with it. `POST` answers `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`.

The delete removed one package's row, then dropped the object's storage without asking whether a row of the object remains. The remaining package's object keeps its definition and loses its data.

## What done looks like

- A per-package delete that leaves another row of the object stored never drops the object's storage. The owning seat chooses one remedy: refuse `dropStorage=true` while another row remains, with a prescription, or skip the drop and say so in the receipt. A loud refusal is the stricter shape, but the choice is the seat's.
- A pin on a real kernel: two packages hold an object, `DELETE ...?package=P&dropStorage=true`, and Q's records survive. The negative control is that the last row's delete with `dropStorage=true` still drops the table.

## Family

The package-axis delete family of #23297 (PR #23408 fixes the registry heal after the same per-package delete; it does not touch the storage drop). #23165 (closed) made the delete name its package.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on this repo, closed included: `dropStorage per-package delete drops table while another package row remains data loss` gives 7 hits.
- #23297 (open) is the family card.
- #23299, #23399 and #10240 are other delete or drop paths: a permission-set row, organization-column drops, attachment tombstoning.
- #23165, #7705 and #7557 (closed) are earlier package-axis or uninstall defects.

None is this.

Dedupe words: dropStorage per-package delete remaining row; shouldDropStorage row remains table dropped; DELETE package dropStorage data loss.
